articles.title: Delhi weather: Rain lashes parts of city as IMD issues red alert - Livemint

articles.full_text:
Rain lashed parts of Delhi on Friday, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a red alert for the next few hours as moderate to heavy rainfall is expected across many areas, PTI reported. Some parts of the city, including central Delhi, received light to moderate rain.
The IMD said many areas are likely to receive moderate to heavy rainfall until 5 pm. In view of the forecast, its district-level nowcast has issued a red alert.
Meteorologists said Delhi could also experience light to moderate rain during the evening hours. Rainfall activity is likely to continue across the national capital for the next two days, till Sunday.
Delhi-NCR is likely to see spells of rain over the weekend, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting showers on September 12 and 13, coinciding with the first two days of the summit.
On Saturday, September 12, very light to light rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning is expected at several places from early morning to the forenoon. The weather may turn wetter again later in the day, with another spell of light to moderate rain likely from the evening through the night.
Is Delhi's rain forecast a concern ahead of the BRICS Summit?
The weather warning comes as Delhi prepares for a major diplomatic gathering. The capital will host the 18th BRICS Summit at Bharat Mandapam on September 12 and 13, with India holding the group's chairship this year. The summit is being held under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, which draws on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of “Humanity First” and a people-centric approach.
The two-day event is expected to see the participation of leaders from BRICS member and partner nations, besides countries invited for outreach.
The movement of foreign delegations, diplomatic convoys and thousands of security personnel is expected to intensify across the capital during the summit. Authorities are therefore closely monitoring the weather, as prolonged or heavy rainfall could create challenges for traffic arrangements around Bharat Mandapam and designated VVIP routes. There has, however, been no official indication of any disruption to the summit because of the weather.
Residents have been advised to exercise caution as the city enters a week of heightened security. Traffic police have asked people to avoid waterlogged and low-lying areas and follow weather and traffic advisories.
The expected rainfall is linked to the monsoon axis, which is currently passing over the city, meteorologists said.
“In the north, since the monsoon axis will quickly move down, easterlies will take over from tomorrow (Friday) onwards; parts of Uttar Pradesh, Delhi-NCR, Haryana, Punjab, Chandigarh, and Rajasthan are expected to receive a passing spell of moderate rains in the afternoon and evening hours starting tomorrow (Friday) into the weekend. Although these spells are going to be mostly localised, with general coverage of 30-40%, not everyone in the plains will receive rain from this spell,” meteorologist Navdeep Dahiya was quoted as saying by Hindustan Times.
